summary: Large payments fintech evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private to replace an in-house GPU fleet. Primary focus: deterministic throughput and strict latency SLOs for customer-facing chat and real-time invoice classification; also embeddings for fraud detection. Cost-sensitive but will pay for predictable SLA-backed capacity. Key ask: warm-pool behavior and scale-down safeguards to avoid cold-start latency on peak windows.
technical_requirements: Throughput: 10k qps aggregate for embeddings pipeline (batching expected), 2k qps for chat tier at 95ms p50 target
Latency SLOs: chat 99th <= 350ms, embeddings p95 <= 200ms for medium batches
Reserved GPU planning: initial commit 40x A100-class GPUs with headroom for +30% burst
Scale policies: prefer scale-up in steps of 10 GPUs within 3 minutes; scale-down conservative (cooldown 30m) to avoid evicting warm KV caches
Warm pools: maintain a warm pool sized to cover first-minute burst per service, separate pools for chat vs embeddings
Queueing: hard max queue depth and prioritized routing (chat high priority), circuit-breaker for degraded backends
Fallbacks: automatic routing to smaller quantized variants on overload, fallback to hosted low-cost model for non-sensitive workloads

poc_plan: Phase 1: 2-week smoke test on Dedicated 8-GPU pool with representative chat traffic (goal: validate p50/p95 latency)
Phase 2: Load test week - ramp to 120% expected peak for 48 hours to measure autoscaling and queueing behaviors
Phase 3: Warm-pool tuning - iterate warm pool sizes to eliminate cold-starts on predictable windows
Phase 4: Failure runs - simulate node drains and region fallback; measure degradation and recovery time
poc_metrics: Sustained throughput without dropped requests at 110% peak
Autoscale reaction time: add capacity within 3 minutes under sustained load
Scale-down should not evict >20% of hot KV caches in cooldown window
No more than 0.1% requests routed to fallback in normal load
